source_evidence: Your adviser will provide you with a brochure containing important information about its advisory business before or at the time you enter into an advisory agreement. Your adviser will also provide you with a “relationship summary.”
answer: Before you open an investment advisory account, expect to receive two disclosure documents. The adviser’s brochure describes its advisory business, including how it is compensated, its fee schedule, whether fees are negotiable, and potential conflicts of interest. The relationship summary gives a concise overview of the services offered, their fees and costs, potential conflicts, the required standard of conduct, legal or disciplinary history, and questions you can ask. Review both documents and ask the adviser to explain anything you do not understand before entering into an agreement.
